info.title: BytNode Crypto Market Data API
info.summary: Crypto market data aggregated across the major venues, derivatives, order flow, options, macro, ETF and on-chain — for developers and AI agents.
info.description:
**BytNode is a crypto market-data API built for developers and AI agents.** One key gives you market data aggregated across the major crypto venues, derivatives positioning, order flow, options, macro, ETF and on-chain fundamentals — about 120 REST routes, a consolidated real-time WebSocket and a native MCP server, all behind one consistent contract.

## Why BytNode

- **Aggregated across the major venues, not one exchange.** Spot and perpetual futures markets are consolidated into one number per metric: volumes are summed, rates are open-interest weighted, prices volume weighted — and the method is documented for every metric, with the number of contributing venues on every row (`venue_count`).
- **Depth on the assets that matter.** 22 pairs: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE, BNB, TRX, SUI, HYPE, XLM, XMR, LINK, ADA, LTC, UNI, GRAM (ex-TON), AVAX, HBAR, NEAR, TAO, plus USDC and USDT spot pairs. This is a deliberate choice: together these assets are about 93 % of the total crypto market capitalisation (measured on 2026-09-30: 2.69 of 2.88 trillion USD), and each of them gets every family of data from every venue that lists it — quality and depth on the assets people actually trade, instead of thin coverage of thousands of tickers.
- **Twelve data families in one API.** Prices and candles, individual trades, order book, order flow (CVD, trade candles), funding, basis, open interest, liquidations and liquidation heatmap, tokenomics, sentiment, macro (FRED + intraday), spot ETF fundamentals (SEC EDGAR), options (OI, IV, max pain, greeks), Bitcoin network, Ethereum fundamentals, on-chain valuation, and 19 server-side technical indicators. Many providers sell these as separate products; here they share one key, one envelope and one set of conventions.
- **Honest numbers.** Every bucketed value says whether it is final (`is_closed`); every multi-venue metric says how many venues contributed (`venue_count`, `coverage`); every empty answer says why (`unavailable`: `not_applicable`, `no_api_key`, `no_data`); every numeric field has a documented unit.
- **Made for AI agents.** A native MCP server (3 tools, 61 fields), `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`, this OpenAPI contract with units and real examples, one-request snapshots of up to 49 fields, and stable machine-readable error codes.
- **Priced for builders.** A free plan (10,000 requests/month), then Traders from 6.95 USD/month, Financial from 19.95 USD/month and Startup from 99.95 USD/month (billed yearly), with history depth and families growing with the plan. See https://bytnode.com/pricing.

## Quick start

1. Create a free key at https://bytnode.com/sign-up.
2. Send it in the `X-API-KEY` header:

```
curl -H "X-API-KEY: $BYTNODE_API_KEY" "https://api.bytnode.com/v1/funding/rate?symbol=BTCUSDT"
```

## Conventions

- **Envelope.** Every success is `{status: "ok", server_time, data_type, data}`, plus the effective `symbol`, `timeframe`, `asset`, `series` or `market` when the route has them. The shape of `data` follows the path: an OBJECT (or `null`) for the latest value of a metric; a LIST (most recent first, or oldest first with `order=asc`) for every `/history` route and every series route — `/v1/klines`, `/v1/ticks/*`, `/v1/trades/futures/seconds`, `/v1/liquidations/events`, which are series by nature (candles, ticks, events, one row per second). Collections are lists too: `/v1/symbols`, `/v1/etf/fundamentals`, `/v1/macro/series`, `/v1/macro/intraday/series`, and the options expiry, max-pain and OI distribution routes. A field that can be `null` is typed so in the schema; any other field is never `null`.
- **Units.** `*_pct` = percent (58.5 = 58.5 %), `*_ratio` = fraction (0.585), `*_bps` = basis points, `*_usd` = USD (every USD amount ends in `_usd`), `*_s` = seconds, `*_pp` = percentage points. Prices are in the quote currency (USDT for BTCUSDT). Volumes and quantities (`volume`, `buy_volume`, `sell_volume`, `net_volume`, `oi_total`...) are in BASE ASSET units (BTC for BTCUSDT), never dollars: a quantity without a unit suffix is in base asset units. A candle names the market of each volume: `volume_spot` (summed across venues), `volume_futures` (perpetuals) and `volume_total` (both). Every response schema carries each field's unit in `x-unit`. Numbers are rounded to 12 significant digits.
- **Names.** One concept has one name on every route, in the snapshot, in the MCP and on the WebSocket: `buy_volume` / `sell_volume` / `net_volume`, `trade_count`, `venue_count`, `sample_count`, booleans `is_*`, a qualitative reading `label`, instants `*_at`, durations `*_s`; the perpetual market is `futures` everywhere. `data_type` is the route's own name (`/v1/trades/avg-size/history` -> `trades_avg_size_history`), and a snapshot field is named after the route that serves the same data (`liquidations_cumulative`, `trades@1h`). Every retired name and its replacement is listed in `x-renamed` at the root of this contract.
- **Time.** Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds (`2026-09-28T14:00:00.000Z`). `time` is the canonical key: every timestamped object under `data` carries it. It follows ONE of two rules, and the description of `time` on each route says which. (1) A row of a BUCKETED series (candles, trade candles, CVD, order book per bucket, funding per 8-hour period, every `/history` read with `timeframe`) is dated at the START of its bucket. (2) A POINT-IN-TIME value is dated at the instant it refers to: the END of a rolling window (`/v1/buysell/ratio`, `/v1/liquidations/cumulative`, `/v1/oi/delta`), the instant of the computation (`/v1/basis`), the instant the SOURCE states (options, BTC, ETH, tokenomics; `/v1/global`, which may end in `.999`), the settlement a forecast is for (`/v1/funding/next`), the EVENT (ticks, large trades, liquidations), and the most recent input of a composite (`/v1/macro/correlations`, `/momentum`, `/risk`, which also give `oldest_input_date` and a `time` per component). A daily value is dated at midnight UTC. The envelope's `server_time` is the time of the response. Time bounds (`since_ms`, `until_ms`) are epoch MILLISECONDS, inclusive.
- **Closed buckets.** Bucketed routes serve the last CLOSED bucket; `?live=1` adds the open one with `is_closed: false`.
- **Freshness.** A response is never more than 1 second old (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=1`). `x-update-frequency-seconds` on each operation says how often the SOURCE changes — from 2 s (ticks) to 5 min (daily macro, on-chain, ETF series): polling faster than that returns the same values.
- **Strict parameters.** An undeclared or repeated parameter is a 422 with a suggestion (`limt` -> did you mean `limit`?). `?fields=a,b.c` projects `data`.
- **Aggregation only.** No route discloses which venue a number came from, except the inter-venue spread, whose purpose is to compare venues.

## Errors

Every error has one shape:

```
{"status": "error", "server_time": "2026-09-30T14:07:27.808Z",
 "error": {"code": "invalid_symbol", "message": "Unknown symbol 'BTCUSD'. Accepted values: ...", "param": "symbol"}}
```

Branch on `error.code` (stable, listed in the `Error` schema), show `error.message` (English). Plan refusals also carry an `X-Deny-Reason` header (`key`, `family`, `websocket`, `rate`, `quota`, `depth`); 429 and 503 carry `Retry-After`.

## Limits

Each plan has a per-minute rate, a monthly quota and a history window per timeframe. Responses made with a metered key carry the IETF `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` headers. Going further back than your plan allows is a 403 `history_depth`, never a silently truncated answer. Details: https://bytnode.com/docs/rate-limits.

## Versioning

The contract is `v1`. Adding routes, fields or parameters is not a breaking change. A breaking change is announced in the changelog (https://bytnode.com/docs/changelog) with notice by plan: Traders 30 days, Financial 60 days, Startup 90 days, Enterprise per contract.

## Links

Docs https://bytnode.com/docs · Pricing https://bytnode.com/pricing · Full reference for LLMs https://bytnode.com/llms-full.txt · WebSocket `wss://api.bytnode.com/ws` · MCP `https://api.bytnode.com/mcp` · Contact contact@bytnode.com

tags.name: System
tags.description: Health, per-feed freshness, the list of served symbols and what each symbol supports. `/v1/health` is the only route that needs no key.

tags.name: Snapshot
tags.description: One request, up to 49 fields for one symbol: the fastest way to fill a dashboard or give an AI agent full market context. Each field is `name=depth` (`funding_rate=1`, or `true` for depth 1); multi-timeframe fields are `name@tf=depth` (`klines@1h=24`, `cvd@1h=24`). Call it with only `symbol` to list the fields your plan includes.

tags.name: Market: prices & volumes
tags.description: OHLCV candles, individual trades, price change and the aggregated order book. OHLC comes from one reference spot market per symbol; a candle names the market of each volume: `volume_spot` (summed across venues), `volume_futures` (perpetuals) and `volume_total` (both).

tags.name: Order flow
tags.description: Who is buying and who is selling: trade candles (spot, futures, combined), CVD, buy/sell ratio, average trade size and inter-venue spread. Every bucketed series says whether the value is final (`is_closed`).

tags.name: Derivatives
tags.description: Perpetual futures positioning, aggregated across venues: funding (settled, estimated, cumulative), basis, open interest.

tags.name: Liquidations
tags.description: Forced liquidations across venues: individual events, cumulative long/short USD, big vs small liquidations, and the liquidation heatmap clusters the price is drawn to.

tags.name: Tokenomics & sentiment
tags.description: Supply, market cap and FDV derived from the live price; total crypto market cap and dominance; the Crypto Fear & Greed Index.

tags.name: Macro
tags.description: Daily FRED series (rates, inflation, liquidity, commodities), intraday macro candles (DXY, EUR/USD, gold, oil, US yields, VIX...), and derived crypto-macro signals: net liquidity, BTC correlations, macro momentum, risk-on/risk-off score.

tags.name: ETF
tags.description: Spot BTC and ETH ETF fundamentals per issuer, anchored on SEC EDGAR filings: shares, NAV, net assets and coins held.

tags.name: Options
tags.description: BTC and ETH options aggregated across venues: open interest and volume (calls/puts, USD), put/call ratio, ATM implied volatility, max pain, per-expiry and per-strike views, OI-weighted greeks.

tags.name: Bitcoin network
tags.description: Bitcoin chain state: recommended fees, mempool, mining pool concentration, difficulty and the next adjustment.

tags.name: Ethereum
tags.description: Ethereum fundamentals: gas, supply and burn, staking and yield, DeFi TVL, ETH/BTC ratio and derived signals (deflation, supply squeeze, gas momentum).

tags.name: On-chain Bitcoin
tags.description: Daily on-chain valuation and activity: MVRV, NVT, active addresses, miner stress.

tags.name: Technical indicators
tags.description: 19 technical indicators computed server-side on the same candles as `/v1/klines`, several per request (RSI, MACD, Bollinger, ATR, Ichimoku...).

server_time.description: Server time of the response, ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds, in the format of every date of `data`. It is not the time of the data: rows carry their own `time`.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable code. Branch on it, never on the message.

- `depth_too_large`: A snapshot field depth exceeds its documented maximum.
- `edge_rate_limited`: Too many simultaneous requests from this IP address (edge anti-flood).
- `history_depth`: The requested history goes further back than your plan allows.
- `insufficient_data`: Not enough history to compute the requested indicator.
- `internal_error`: Unexpected server error. Not worth retrying immediately.
- `invalid_api_key`: The API key is missing, invalid or revoked.
- `invalid_asset`: The asset is not served by this family. The error lists the accepted values.
- `invalid_depth`: A snapshot field depth is not a positive integer.
- `invalid_exchange`: The exchange value is not accepted.
- `invalid_indicator`: The POST /v1/indicators body is invalid (id, type or parameters).
- `invalid_pair`: The pair value is not accepted.
- `invalid_parameter`: A parameter has an invalid type or value.
- `invalid_series`: The macro series does not exist. See the family's /series catalogue.
- `invalid_symbol`: The symbol is not served. The error lists the accepted values (see /v1/symbols).
- `invalid_time_range`: since_ms / until_ms are not valid epoch milliseconds, or since_ms >= until_ms.
- `invalid_timeframe`: The timeframe is not accepted by this route.
- `method_not_allowed`: The route exists but not with this HTTP method.
- `missing_expiry`: The route needs an options expiry; the error lists the active ones.
- `missing_parameter`: A required parameter is missing.
- `not_applicable`: The request has no meaning for this asset (e.g. indicators on a stablecoin).
- `not_found`: Unknown route.
- `plan_family`: Your plan does not include this data family.
- `plan_websocket`: Your plan does not include the WebSocket stream.
- `quota_exceeded`: Your plan's monthly quota is exhausted.
- `rate_limited`: Your plan's per-minute rate is exceeded. Retry after Retry-After seconds.
- `repeated_parameter`: A parameter appears more than once.
- `service_unavailable`: Temporary unavailability. Retry after Retry-After seconds.
- `timeframe_not_served`: The series exists but does not serve this timeframe.
- `unknown_field`: A ?fields= or snapshot field name does not exist.
- `unknown_parameter`: The route does not declare this parameter.
- `upstream_timeout`: The request took too long. Reduce the window or depth, then retry.

param.description: The parameter at fault, when there is one.

Unauthorized.description: The API key is missing, invalid or revoked (`invalid_api_key`). Send it in the `X-API-KEY` header.

error.message: API key missing, invalid or revoked. Send it in the X-API-KEY header; create one at https://bytnode.com/dashboard/keys.

Forbidden.description: The key is valid but your plan does not cover the request (`plan_family`, `plan_websocket`, `history_depth`).

error.message: History depth beyond your plan: 30 day(s) requested on 1h, your plan allows 1 day(s) (i.e. at most limit=24 on this timeframe, and no since_ms/until_ms bound beyond that window).

NotFound.description: Unknown route (`not_found`). A removed or renamed route names its replacement in the message.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The route exists, but not with this HTTP method (`method_not_allowed`). `Allow` lists the accepted ones.

Unprocessable.description: A parameter is missing, unknown, repeated or has an invalid value (`missing_parameter`, `unknown_parameter`, `repeated_parameter`, `invalid_parameter`, `invalid_symbol`, `invalid_asset`, `invalid_series`, `invalid_timeframe`, `invalid_time_range`, `invalid_depth`, `depth_too_large`, `invalid_indicator`, `unknown_field`...).

error.message: Unknown symbol 'BTCUSD'. Accepted values: ADAUSDT, AVAXUSDT, BNBUSDT, BTCUSDT, ...
Unknown parameter 'limt'. Did you mean 'limit'? Accepted parameters: fields, limit, since_ms, symbol, timeframe, until_ms.
since_ms=1790000000 looks like seconds: time bounds are epoch MILLISECONDS (e.g. since_ms=1790000000000).

TooManyRequests.description: Your plan's per-minute rate (`rate_limited`) or monthly quota (`quota_exceeded`) is exhausted, or too many simultaneous requests from one IP (`edge_rate_limited`).

error.message: Rate limit exceeded: your plan allows a limited number of requests per minute. Retry after the Retry-After delay.

RateLimit-Policy.description: Your plan's rate and quota (IETF draft).
Your plan's rate and quota (IETF draft).

Cache-Control.description: `private, max-age=1` at most: no response is served more than one second old. How often the SOURCE of a route changes is its `x-update-frequency-seconds`; polling faster than that returns the same values.

APIKeyHeader.name: X-API-KEY
APIKeyHeader.description: Your API key (`cb_live_...`). Get a free one at https://bytnode.com/sign-up.

get.description: Perpetual futures price versus spot, OI-weighted across venues (each venue weighted by its latest open interest within 10 minutes). An INSTANT value, not a window: each venue's last futures and spot trade prices (at most 2 minutes old) at `time`.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Trading pair, e.g. `BTCUSDT`. Required. The 22 served pairs: `GET /v1/symbols`. Case-insensitive (`btcusdt` works; the envelope gives the canonical `BTCUSDT`). An unknown pair returns 422 `invalid_symbol` with the accepted list.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated projection of `data` (dot notation for nested keys): `fields=time,basis_pct`. Unknown field: 422 `unknown_field` with a suggestion.

200.description: Success. The example is a real response, trimmed to 3 rows.

server_time.description: Server time of the response, ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds, in the format of every date of `data`. It is not the time of the data: rows carry their own `time`.

time.description: Point-in-time value: the instant of the venue prices used (each venue's last futures and spot trades, at most 2 minutes old).

basis_pct.description: (futures - spot) / spot, in percent. Positive = contango.

futures_price.description: Perpetual futures price, open-interest weighted across venues.

data.description: The payload. Most recent first when it is a list.

unavailable.description: Present only when `data` is empty: why. `not_applicable` = the metric does not exist for this asset (e.g. futures on a stablecoin); `no_api_key` = the upstream source is not wired; `no_data` = nothing measured in the window.

x-codeSamples.label: Python
x-codeSamples.source:
import os, requests

r = requests.get(
    "https://api.bytnode.com/v1/basis",
    params={"symbol": "BTCUSDT"},
    headers={"X-API-KEY": os.environ["BYTNODE_API_KEY"]},
    timeout=30,
)
r.raise_for_status()
print(r.json()["data"])

get.description: One row per closed bucket of `timeframe` (required). Most recent first, or oldest first with `order=asc`. Follow `next` to read the following page (it never repeats a row).

parameters.name: since_ms
parameters.description: Lower time bound, INCLUSIVE, in epoch MILLISECONDS (13 digits). A value in seconds returns 422 `invalid_time_range`.

parameters.name: until_ms
parameters.description: Upper time bound, INCLUSIVE to the millisecond, in epoch milliseconds. To page, prefer `before_ms` (exclusive) or simply follow `next`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of rows to return, in the reading order (most recent first by default). Also bounded by your plan's history window (403 `history_depth` beyond it).

parameters.name: timeframe
parameters.description: Required: `1m`, `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `4h` or `1d`. One row per closed bucket, aggregating its minutes (`sample_count` = minutes in the bucket); `1m` gives one row per minute, aligned on the minute. Missing: 422 `missing_parameter`.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Trading pair, e.g. `BTCUSDT`. Required. The 22 served pairs: `GET /v1/symbols`. Case-insensitive (`btcusdt` works; the envelope gives the canonical `BTCUSDT`). An unknown pair returns 422 `invalid_symbol` with the accepted list.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated projection of `data` (dot notation for nested keys): `fields=time,basis_pct`. Unknown field: 422 `unknown_field` with a suggestion.

parameters.name: before_ms
parameters.description: Upper time bound, EXCLUSIVE, in epoch milliseconds: rows strictly before it. Pass the oldest `time` you received to read the previous page without repeating a row. Not combinable with `until_ms` (422 `invalid_time_range`).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Reading order: `desc` (most recent first, the default) or `asc` (oldest first, reading forward from `since_ms`, which is then required). Follow `next` to read the following page.

200.description: Success. The example is a real response, trimmed to 3 rows.

server_time.description: Server time of the response, ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds, in the format of every date of `data`. It is not the time of the data: rows carry their own `time`.

time.description: Without `timeframe`: the instant of the one-minute measurement. With `timeframe`: start of the bucket, the value aggregating the bucket's minutes.

basis_pct.description: (futures - spot) / spot, in percent. Positive = contango.

futures_price.description: Perpetual futures price, open-interest weighted across venues.

sample_count.description: Number of source points behind the value (one-minute points in a bucket).

is_closed.description: `true` = the bucket is final and will never change; `false` = provisional (only with `?live=1`).

data.description: The payload. Most recent first when it is a list.

next.description: The parameters of the following page — send them in place of your `since_ms` / `until_ms` / `before_ms` / `order`, omitting the null ones (keep `symbol`, `limit`, `timeframe`...). It never repeats a row. `null` once the range is read (the page was not full).

unavailable.description: Present only when `data` is empty: why. `not_applicable` = the metric does not exist for this asset (e.g. futures on a stablecoin); `no_api_key` = the upstream source is not wired; `no_data` = nothing measured in the window.

parameters.description: Bucket size, required: `1m`, `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `4h` or `1d`. Missing: 422 `missing_parameter`; other values: 422 `invalid_timeframe` with the accepted list.

parameters.name: since_ms
parameters.description: Lower time bound, INCLUSIVE, in epoch MILLISECONDS (13 digits). A value in seconds returns 422 `invalid_time_range`.

parameters.name: until_ms
parameters.description: Upper time bound, INCLUSIVE to the millisecond, in epoch milliseconds. To page, prefer `before_ms` (exclusive) or simply follow `next`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of rows to return, in the reading order (most recent first by default). Also bounded by your plan's history window (403 `history_depth` beyond it).

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: Market: `all` (spot + perpetual futures, default), `spot` or `futures`. Other values: 422 `invalid_parameter`.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Trading pair, e.g. `BTCUSDT`. Required. The 22 served pairs: `GET /v1/symbols`. Case-insensitive (`btcusdt` works; the envelope gives the canonical `BTCUSDT`). An unknown pair returns 422 `invalid_symbol` with the accepted list.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated projection of `data` (dot notation for nested keys): `fields=time,basis_pct`. Unknown field: 422 `unknown_field` with a suggestion.

parameters.name: before_ms
parameters.description: Upper time bound, EXCLUSIVE, in epoch milliseconds: rows strictly before it. Pass the oldest `time` you received to read the previous page without repeating a row. Not combinable with `until_ms` (422 `invalid_time_range`).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Reading order: `desc` (most recent first, the default) or `asc` (oldest first, reading forward from `since_ms`, which is then required). Follow `next` to read the following page.

200.description: Success. The example is a real response, trimmed to 3 rows.

server_time.description: Server time of the response, ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds, in the format of every date of `data`. It is not the time of the data: rows carry their own `time`.

market.description: Effective market of the request: `futures` or `spot` (order book), or `all`, `spot`, `futures` (flow routes).

time.description: Start of the bucket the row covers: a 1h bucket at 14:00 covers 14:00:00 to 14:59:59.999.

cvd_series.description: Cumulative volume delta inside the bucket, one point per minute, starting from 0 at the bucket start.

net_volume.description: buy_volume - sell_volume over the row, base asset units. Positive = net buying.

buy_volume.description: Aggressive (taker) buy volume, base asset units, aggregated across venues.

sell_volume.description: Aggressive (taker) sell volume, base asset units, aggregated across venues.

is_volume_estimated.description: `true` when base-asset quantities of this row were ESTIMATED from USD amounts ÷ the candle's typical price (high + low + close) / 3 (data written before quantities were recorded; mean error 0.04 % in 1m, 0.37 % in 1d); `false` = measured.

is_closed.description: `true` = the bucket is final and will never change; `false` = provisional (only with `?live=1`).

data.description: The payload. Most recent first when it is a list.

next.description: The parameters of the following page — send them in place of your `since_ms` / `until_ms` / `before_ms` / `order`, omitting the null ones (keep `symbol`, `limit`, `timeframe`...). It never repeats a row. `null` once the range is read (the page was not full).

unavailable.description: Present only when `data` is empty: why. `not_applicable` = the metric does not exist for this asset (e.g. futures on a stablecoin); `no_api_key` = the upstream source is not wired; `no_data` = nothing measured in the window.

window_s.description: Length of the window, in seconds (86400 = 24 hours).

get.summary: Many fields for one symbol in one request
get.description: 49 fields for one symbol in a single call (41 plain, 8 multi-timeframe): prices, flow, derivatives, liquidations, macro, on-chain, options. Each query key is a field and its value a depth: `funding_rate=1` (or `=true`). Multi-timeframe fields take `@tf`: `klines@1h=24`, `cvd@1h=24`; `klines` also takes `1w`. Every field has the name and the rows of its route. Call it with only `symbol` to get `available_fields` (fields without a timeframe), `available_multi_tf_fields`, `timeframes`, `timeframes_by_field` and `max_depth`. An empty field carries `unavailable` (`not_applicable`, `no_api_key` or `no_data`) so 'no measure' is never mistaken for 'nothing happened'. Most recent first, or oldest first with `order=asc`. Follow `next` to read the following page (it never repeats a row).

parameters.name: since_ms
parameters.description: Lower time bound, INCLUSIVE, in epoch MILLISECONDS (13 digits). A value in seconds returns 422 `invalid_time_range`.

parameters.name: until_ms
parameters.description: Upper time bound, INCLUSIVE to the millisecond, in epoch milliseconds. To page, prefer `before_ms` (exclusive) or simply follow `next`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of rows to return, in the reading order (most recent first by default). Also bounded by your plan's history window (403 `history_depth` beyond it).

parameters.name: timeframe
parameters.description: Required: `1m`, `5m`, `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `4h` or `1d`. One row per closed bucket, aggregating its minutes (`sample_count` = minutes in the bucket); `1m` gives one row per minute, aligned on the minute. Missing: 422 `missing_parameter`.

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: Market: `all` (spot + perpetual futures, default), `spot` or `futures`. Other values: 422 `invalid_parameter`.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Trading pair, e.g. `BTCUSDT`. Required. The 22 served pairs: `GET /v1/symbols`. Case-insensitive (`btcusdt` works; the envelope gives the canonical `BTCUSDT`). An unknown pair returns 422 `invalid_symbol` with the accepted list.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated projection of `data` (dot notation for nested keys): `fields=time,basis_pct`. Unknown field: 422 `unknown_field` with a suggestion.

parameters.name: before_ms
parameters.description: Upper time bound, EXCLUSIVE, in epoch milliseconds: rows strictly before it. Pass the oldest `time` you received to read the previous page without repeating a row. Not combinable with `until_ms` (422 `invalid_time_range`).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Reading order: `desc` (most recent first, the default) or `asc` (oldest first, reading forward from `since_ms`, which is then required). Follow `next` to read the following page.

200.description: Success. The example is a real response, trimmed to 3 rows.

server_time.description: Server time of the response, ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds, in the format of every date of `data`. It is not the time of the data: rows carry their own `time`.

market.description: Effective market of the request: `futures` or `spot` (order book), or `all`, `spot`, `futures` (flow routes).

time.description: Without `timeframe`: start of the one-minute candle. With `timeframe`: start of the bucket the row covers: a 1h bucket at 14:00 covers 14:00:00 to 14:59:59.999.

avg_trade_size.description: Average trade size, base asset units (NOT dollars: multiply by the price for a notional).

volume.description: Traded volume over the row, base asset units (BTC for BTCUSDT, NOT dollars), aggregated across venues.

is_volume_estimated.description: `true` when base-asset quantities of this row were ESTIMATED from USD amounts ÷ the candle's typical price (high + low + close) / 3 (data written before quantities were recorded; mean error 0.04 % in 1m, 0.37 % in 1d); `false` = measured.

sample_count.description: Number of source points behind the value (one-minute points in a bucket).

is_closed.description: `true` = the bucket is final and will never change; `false` = provisional (only with `?live=1`).

data.description: The payload. Most recent first when it is a list.

next.description: The parameters of the following page — send them in place of your `since_ms` / `until_ms` / `before_ms` / `order`, omitting the null ones (keep `symbol`, `limit`, `timeframe`...). It never repeats a row. `null` once the range is read (the page was not full).

unavailable.description: Present only when `data` is empty: why. `not_applicable` = the metric does not exist for this asset (e.g. futures on a stablecoin); `no_api_key` = the upstream source is not wired; `no_data` = nothing measured in the window.

x-codeSamples.label: Python
x-codeSamples.source:
import os, requests

r = requests.get(
    "https://api.bytnode.com/v1/trades/spot/history",
    params={"symbol": "BTCUSDT", "timeframe": "1h", "limit": "3"},
    headers={"X-API-KEY": os.environ["BYTNODE_API_KEY"]},
    timeout=30,
)
r.raise_for_status()
print(r.json()["data"])
